issue.title: Screen reader just says "button" on the event page
body: I use a screen reader. On the Friday Community Night page, the logo link at the top is announced only as "link", so I don't know where it goes.
Under the event there are three round buttons. Two of them have names, but the first one is just "button". I wanted to donate and had to guess.

task.instruction: Select "Move focus into the page" and Tab through it while watching the screen reader view. Find the donate button and press Enter.
task.afterReproduce: Without names, the logo link and the donate button are guesswork. Give them accessible names.

fixes.title: Header: the logo image inside the home link

options.label: Add alt="logo"
options.feedback: The checks pass, but "logo" describes the picture, not where the link goes. For an image that is the only content of a link, the alt text should be the link's purpose.

options.label: Add alt="" to mark the image as decorative
options.feedback: Empty alt is right for decorative images, but this image is the only content of the link, so the link now has no name at all.

options.label: Add alt="Commons Community Center home"
options.feedback: The link now says who it belongs to and where it goes.

options.label: Add data-label="Donate"
options.feedback: Assistive technology doesn't read data- attributes, so the button is still unnamed.

options.label: Add aria-hidden="true" so the unlabeled button stops being announced
options.feedback: Now the button is still focusable but announces nothing, which is worse. Hiding a control doesn't fix it.

options.label: Add aria-label="Donate"
options.feedback: The button is now announced as "Donate, button". A visible text label would help even more people, including voice control users.

merged.reply: Perfect, the logo says where it goes and the first button says "Donate". Just made my donation for Friday.
learn: Every image needs a text alternative. When the image is the only content of a link, describe where the link goes.
Icon-only buttons need an accessible name, for example aria-label.
Never use aria-hidden on something that can receive focus.
